concept.name: Head and shoulders
concept.definition: A classical technical-analysis reversal pattern consisting of three successive peaks in which the middle peak (the head) is the highest and the two outside peaks (the shoulders) are lower and roughly equal, with the intervening reaction lows connected by a neckline. The pattern is treated as complete — and the prior uptrend tentatively reversed — only when price breaks below the neckline. It is an analytical framework for reading supply/demand shifts, not a proven predictive law.
concept.intuition: Buyers make one final push to a new high (the head), but the next rally (the right shoulder) can no longer reach it — a sign that demand is exhausting. When price then breaks the neckline, sellers have taken control.
concept.mechanics: Identify an established uptrend, then three peaks with the middle one highest; draw the neckline through the two reaction lows (it may slope up, down, or be horizontal). Confirmation is a decisive close below the neckline, ideally on expanding volume; a return move to the neckline (support turned resistance) is common. The conventional price target projects the head-to-neckline distance downward from the break point.
concept.formula: Price target = N - (H - N), where H = price at the top of the head and N = neckline price at the breakout point.
concept.failure_modes: The pattern fails when the neckline never breaks (the right shoulder just becomes a higher low in a continuing uptrend) or when the break is a false breakout followed by a rally back above the right-shoulder high. Subjective peak selection and sloppy necklines make many 'patterns' artifacts of the beholder.
concept.misconceptions: That the three peaks alone signal a top — without a neckline break there is no confirmed reversal, and perfectly symmetrical shoulders are not required. It is also wrongly treated as a guaranteed sell signal rather than a probabilistic hypothesis.
concept.example: A stock rallies to $20.50 (left shoulder), pulls back to $17.50, rallies to a new high and falls back to $17.50 (head), then rallies only to $20 (right shoulder). A close below the $17.50 neckline completes the pattern and projects a target near $14.50.
